newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian British Bank bond issue oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian British Bank bond issue oversubscribed.

text.p: Private-sector Egyptian British Bank said on Thursday its 100 million pound ($29 million) bond offer had closed oversubscribed by 16 million pounds.
An official at the bond department told Reuters the bank had closed the offer on December 24 after investors had asked to buy bonds worth 116 million pounds.
"We are happy with the results," the official said, adding that the bonds will be distributed on a pro rata basis.
Under the original timetable, the bond offer would have closed on February 15.
The bonds, worth 1,000 pounds each, are non-convertible and valid for five years. They have a 0.25 percent coupon and yields would be distributed every three months.
Yields are be based on the latest annualised average yield of 91-day treasury bills announced by the Central Bank no more than 14 days before the bond yield is calculated.
On December 25, the yield on 91-day bills fell to 10.059 percent from 10.063 percent at the previous auction.
The bank, in which HSBC Holdings own a 40 percent stake, said it would use the 100 million pounds raised by the issue to finance its activities.
Private sector American Express Bank Egypt, Citibank Egypt and joint venture Egyptian American Bank have also issued bonds during 1996.
